chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so an old man from the people of Iraq spoke to him and said to him, 'Why do I see your speech as changed?' He said to him, 'The front (teeth) of my mouth have fallen off, so my speech is deficient.' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'And I as well, some of my teeth have fallen off, to the extent that Satan whispers to me, saying,

key_terms.الثَّرِيد: Tharid (a traditional dish of bread soaked in broth/meat)
key_terms.لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّه: There is no power and no strength except with Allah (a phrase of patience)
key_terms.مَقَادِمُ فَمِي: front of my mouth (referring to incisors)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq advise regarding diet for the elderly?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in *Al-Kafi*, illustrates the Imam’s relatability to the physical frailties of aging, using the loss of teeth as a metaphor for the weakening of one's capacity to engage in discourse. It highlights the practical Shia tradition of dietary wisdom for the elderly, specifically recommending *tharid* (bread soaked in broth) for ease of consumption while cautioning against heavy fats like *samn*. The narrative underscores the spiritual discipline of patience (*sabr*) against the whispers of Satan regarding material sustenance during times of physical decline.
